E-2 · 2026-07-18engine 2026-07-18-exempt-events-rou-horizon-cpi-scopedec-v1
Affected: exempt-lease-subsequent-events, reassessment-and-term-shorten-ROU-depreciation-horizon, scope-decrease-same-day-CPI-rebase

Three corrections to how the calculator handles changes made after a lease has started. First, on a lease you have put on the short-term or low-value exemption, a later change is no longer left out in silence. If you extend or shorten the term, the straight-line expense is re-spread over the revised term. If you record a price-index change, a rent renegotiation, a residual value guarantee or a make-good provision on an exempt lease, the calculator now raises an action-required note explaining that the expense shown does not reflect that change, rather than quietly ignoring it, and a workbook with such a note can no longer certify as ready. A short-term lease whose revised term goes over twelve months, or that gains a purchase option, is flagged as no longer qualifying for the short-term exemption. Second, when a lease-term reassessment or a term-shortening change brings the lease end forward (for example a break option that becomes reasonably certain), the right-of-use asset now finishes depreciating at the revised lease end instead of carrying a value past the actual end of the lease. Third, the same-day index re-base that already applied to a rent renegotiation now also applies when the rent is renegotiated through a scope reduction, so recording a price-index reading on the day you reduce the scope no longer stacks that day's uplift on top of the newly agreed rent.

E-A (IFRS 16.5-16.7, 16.6; ruling R26 with Amendment A, L2 + L4 + cross-challenge; search_ifrs16 verified 2026-07-18: 16.5 opts a lease out of paragraphs 22-49, 16.6 straight-lines the payments over the lease term). An exempt lease has no liability, so the 16.40-46 remeasurement machinery does not apply and a subsequent event flows through the 16.6 straight-line expense. The exempt branch (runExemptLease) previously dropped CPI, modification, reassessment and residual-value-guarantee inputs with no warning, mis-stating the expense while still certifying READY. It now: (1) re-spreads the 16.6 expense over the revised term for a clean flat-rent term change (representative: r006 low-value, term extended 31.12.2033 -> 31.12.2036, expense 400,000 over 120 months -> 520,000 over 156 months at 3,333.33/month); (2) raises the existing EXEMPTION_SHORT_TERM_OVER_12_MONTHS BLOCKING exception when a term change takes a short-term lease over 12 months or adds a purchase option, re-tested at the change date (IFRS 16.7, supplied via L4 practice from ifrs.org 2025 primary text + BDO Australia; not returned by the paragraph RAG, so cited by provenance not as a RAG hit); (3) raises EXEMPTION_EVENTS_IGNORED at ACTION_REQUIRED severity for every other un-applied event (CPI, consideration or scope change, RVG, restoration, or a term change tangled with a payment/CPI/scope change), so the export certification gate refuses READY (Amendment A: a REVIEW-severity note would auto-resolve to Completed and let a mis-stated figure ship) and the message states the expense excludes the event. RVG timing and the low-value multi-year CPI re-spread have no published guidance (L4-verified), so the engine warns rather than inventing a convention. Workbook resolution verified: g04b (low-value + CPI) -> ACTION_REQUIRED, r006 (term applied) -> REVIEW_RECOMMENDED, clean exempt lease with no event -> READY_FOR_REPORTING and byte-identical (negative control). E-C (IFRS 16.32, search_ifrs16 verified 2026-07-18: 'Otherwise, the lessee shall depreciate the right-of-use asset from the commencement date to the earlier of the end of the useful life of the right-of-use asset or the end of the lease term'). When an applied lease-term reassessment or a term-shortening modification brings the lease end forward, the right-of-use asset now depreciates to the revised lease end. The useful-life decouple (depreciating past the lease end) is gated on a reasonably-certain purchase option, since only then does the lessee keep the asset; a non-purchase-option lease amortises to the earlier of useful life and the revised lease term. Representative: r005 (break option reasonably certain, RVG 47,000, no purchase option, break 31.12.2027) closing right-of-use asset at the break 26,471.39 -> 0.00, phantom depreciation to 31.12.2032 removed, revised remaining amount 30,442.10 re-spread over 9 months at 3,382.46/month. A purchase-option lease still depreciates past the lease end over the asset useful life (byte-identical control). E-B (IFRS 16.42, 16.45; extends BF-29). The same-day index re-base that suppressed a spurious CPI uplift on a same-day consideration change now also covers a scope-decrease that renegotiates the rent to an explicit flat amount. Representative: g05 (scope decrease to 15,833 with a same-day index 84) payment 13,299.72 -> 15,833.00, post-modification opening liability 68,272.04 -> 81,276.24, same-day CPI delta 0. Fenced: a scope decrease followed by a genuinely later CPI still reprices (15,833 -> 17,416.30 at index 110), and a consideration-change same-day CPI is byte-identical to BF-29. FROZEN-HISTORY NOTE: the E-C and E-B engine changes were committed on 2026-07-17 (commit 255ed3ff) without a cache-version bump or changelog entry, because their affected scenarios are not in the golden set so the goldens-hash gate did not require one; this entry records them together with E-A and bumps LEASE_ENGINE_CACHE_VERSION so the saved-lease drift advisory reaches any affected user. Golden scenarios unchanged; goldens sha unchanged. Regression oracles (RED-pre / GREEN-post, c109/c110 controls): tests/unit/rou-depreciation-horizon.test.js (E-C), tests/unit/cpi-anchor-rebase.test.js (E-B), tests/unit/exempt-events.test.js (E-A).

E-1 · 2026-07-17engine 2026-07-17-balloon-carry-cpi-rebase-v1
Affected: scope-decrease-with-RVG/PO-balloon, same-day-CPI-with-consideration-mod

Two corrections to how the calculator handles end-of-term amounts and same-day index changes when a lease is modified. First, when a modification reduces the lease scope, any end-of-term amount already in the liability (a residual value guarantee, a purchase-option price, or a termination penalty) is now carried forward in full into the reduced lease and settled at the end, instead of being dropped. Previously the schedule fell to zero at the change date with the guarantee never settled, which understated the liability. If your revised contract reduces the guarantee, you can now enter the revised amount expected to be payable and only the guarantee scales; the purchase-option price and any penalty are never scaled. Second, when you renegotiate the rent to a flat amount and record a consumer-price-index reading on the very same day, the calculator no longer applies that same-day index uplift on top of the newly agreed rent (which double-counted inflation the negotiated rent already reflected); the index anchor re-bases to that day's level, and any later index reading still applies normally. A separate warning was also added (no figures change) flagging the contradiction of a reasonably-certain purchase option held together with a residual value guarantee or a termination penalty.

BF-18 (IFRS 16.27(c)/(d)/(e), 16.42(a)/16.43, 16.45, 16.46(a); ruling R24, L2 money ruling + independent cross-challenge UPHELD): discrete end-of-term balloons carry forward unchanged through a scope-decrease / term-shorten derecognition; default full-persist, RVG scalable only via an explicit revised amount expected to be payable, PO price and penalty never scale. Representative difference (scenario x04, 40% scope decrease, RVG 40,000, revised rate 7.5%): post-modification opening liability 107,764.41 -> 139,962.83 (the 40,000 RVG PV of 32,198.42 was being dropped; understated by 19,319-32,198 depending on whether the guarantee scales). An active REVIEW_REQUIRED prompt is raised at the balloon-present + scope-decrease intersection. BF-29 (IFRS 16.42 anchor re-base): a same-day (at entry) consideration change re-bases the CPI index anchor to that day's level. Representative difference (scenario s23, renegotiate to 11,000 with a same-day index 105): post-modification liability 380,560.46 -> 362,438.53, payments 11,550 -> 11,000. Fenced: a modification followed by a LATER-day CPI (and a mid-month consideration change followed by a later-in-month CPI that only snaps into the same period) is byte-identical to before and reprices normally at the original commencement rate. BF-34/35 (IFRS 16.27(c)/(e)): non-figure-affecting WARN only (measurement unchanged this release; a full fix that excluded the RVG expected-payable and penalty when a purchase option is reasonably certain would move scenario s12 from 565,813.53 to 550,926.54). WBGATE-F2 follow-up (same release): the modification-trace PV evidence (pv_total and pv_table) now includes the carried balloon as a labelled end_of_term_balloon row, so the PerMod PV reconciliation foots to the same post-modification opening the schedule carries (x04 trace pv_total 107,764.41 -> 139,962.83 with a 13th row 40,000 x 0.804961 = 32,198.42; PO path emits its row too; no-balloon modifications byte-identical). Regression oracle: scratchpad/blind-export-review-0717/oracles/rvg-scope-decrease.oracle.js (bite-proven). Golden scenarios unchanged (the published-scope-decrease benchmark has no balloon); goldens sha unchanged.

Baseline entry: the changelog system goes live. The engine reproduces the published worked examples catalogued on the proof page (from the IASB, the major accounting firms, specialist IFRS educators and other software providers), plus checkpoints derived independently from first principles, and passes the full governed suite. The proof page holds the live count and links to every example, so no other page repeats a number; the examples shown there are publicly deep-linkable and the rest run as test oracles only. No figure changes are recorded by this entry; it anchors the enforcement chain.

Figure-affecting changes are recorded here with the affected scenario classes, the size of representative differences, and the reason for the change.

Corrections register

Input-reading and display fixes that did not change the engine

C-9 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Schedule export Depreciation Walkthrough tab (leases whose end date was changed by a modification or reassessment)

Before the end-date change takes effect, the schedules correctly depreciate the right-of-use asset over the lease term that was in force at the time. The Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, which shows the working behind each period's depreciation, instead measured its 'Remaining Frame' on those earlier rows against the revised term. On a shortened lease that understated the frame, so Expected Depreciation ran too high and the Diff columns grew period by period; on an extended lease the frame picked up one month too many. Rows from the change date onwards were always right. As with the purchase-option correction (C-8), the actual depreciation in the ROU schedule, the journals and every balance were always correct; only the walkthrough's explanatory columns disagreed with them. The walkthrough now measures each row against the lease end in force for that row, and the workbook's walkthrough controls fail if the sheet ever disagrees with the schedule again.

Affected input shape: A lease with a modification or reassessment that changed the lease end date (shortened or extended), exported with the Depreciation Walkthrough sheet. The rows before the change date were affected. Window: From the walkthrough sheet going live on 12 June 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for the lease figures: the ROU schedule, journals and balances were always correct. If you exported a lease with an end-date change before 12 July 2026, ignore the Expected Depreciation and Diff columns on the rows before the change on that workbook's Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, or re-export to get a corrected sheet.

C-8 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Schedule export Depreciation Walkthrough tab (purchase-option leases)

On a purchase-option lease the schedules correctly depreciate the right-of-use asset over the asset's useful life rather than the lease term (IFRS 16.32). The Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, which shows the working behind each period's depreciation, wrongly measured its 'Remaining Frame' to the lease end instead of the useful-life end on the in-lease rows. So its Expected Depreciation, Depreciation Diff, Expected Closing ROU and Closing Diff columns were wrong on those rows: the Diff column grew from around one month's depreciation at the start to the entire remaining carrying amount at the final lease period, and Expected Closing ROU showed zero at lease end while the schedule correctly carried the asset into the owned-asset period. The actual depreciation numbers in the ROU schedule, the journals and every balance were always right; only the walkthrough's explanatory columns disagreed with them. The walkthrough now uses the same useful-life horizon as the schedules, and the workbook's walkthrough controls now fail if the walkthrough ever disagrees with the schedule again.

Affected input shape: A lease with a purchase option that is reasonably certain to be exercised and an asset useful life longer than the lease term, exported with the Depreciation Walkthrough sheet. Window: From the purchase-option features going live on 2 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for the lease figures: the ROU schedule, journals and balances were always correct. If you exported a purchase-option lease before 12 July 2026, ignore the Expected Depreciation and Diff columns on that workbook's Depreciation Walkthrough sheet, or re-export to get a corrected sheet.

C-7 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Calculator currency panel (IAS 21 FX Translation view); Schedule export FX Translation tab

For a lease that had been remeasured before the reporting date, the single-lease FX Translation view worked out the derived exchange difference by treating the whole remeasurement uplift as if it were translated at the closing rate. That overstated the exchange gain or loss and routed an amount that belongs to the right-of-use asset (IFRS 16.39) through profit or loss. Working out the exchange difference on a remeasured lease needs the rate on each event date, which this single-rate view does not hold, so it no longer shows a derived exchange difference for these leases: it shows the balances and points to the disclosure note, which translates the lease layer by layer at each event date. Leases with no remeasurement are unchanged, the lease's own-currency schedule was never affected, and the note figure was always right.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease that had been remeasured (a CPI change, a modification or a reassessment) before the reporting date, viewed at a reporting date in the single-lease FX Translation view. Window: From the currency features going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for saved schedules. If you read a derived exchange difference off the FX Translation view or the schedule export's FX Translation tab for a lease that had a CPI change, modification or reassessment before the reporting date, use the disclosure note's figure instead, which translates the lease correctly at each event date.

C-6 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Disclosure note (current and non-current lease liability split); Disclosure workbook

The current portion of the lease liability was worked out as the fall in the balance over the next twelve months. For a lease that is still accruing interest with no payment due in the coming year the balance rises, so this produced a negative current liability. The current portion is the part of the balance due within twelve months (IAS 1.69); when nothing is due in the coming year that part is nil, not a negative number, and the whole balance is non-current. The current portion is now held at nil for such a lease, which is the standard presentation. The total lease liability was always right.

Affected input shape: A lease whose liability grows over the next twelve months, such as a lease in a rent-free period with nothing paid in the coming year. Window: From the disclosure note going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: None for saved schedules. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook showing a negative current lease liability in the window above, generate it again.

C-5 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Disclosure note (presentation-currency note); Disclosure workbook rates sheet

The average rate the note used to translate a year's interest was the average of the reporting month only. For a December year end that was the December average rather than the average across the whole year. Where rates moved through the year this put the interest line on the wrong average, with the difference absorbed into the exchange line, so the note still added up but the split between interest and exchange movement was off. The note now averages across the whole reporting year for the current year, and across the prior year for the comparative, which is the approximation IAS 21.40 intends. The total was always right.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease shown in a presentation-currency note, where the average rate for the year was taken from the reporting month only. Window: From the disclosure note going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: None for saved schedules. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook with a foreign-currency note in the window above, generate it again so the interest and exchange lines use the year's average.

C-4 · 2026-07-12no engine change
Where: Calculator currency panel (IAS 21 view); Schedule export FX Translation tab

The exchange difference on these two views was worked out from the lease start to the reporting date and shown as a single entry to post. At a second or later year end that is the whole difference built up since the lease began, not the difference that arose in the year, so posting it every year would count earlier years again. The panel and the tab now show the exchange difference that arose in the period then ended (the twelve months to the reporting date), with the opening balance carried at the prior year end rate, which is what IAS 21.28 asks you to recognise. Interest for the period is translated at that year's average rather than an average running back to the lease start. Lease schedules in the lease's own currency were never affected, and the first reporting period is unchanged.

Affected input shape: A foreign-currency lease translated at a second or later reporting period, that is, a reporting date more than twelve months after the lease started. Window: From the currency features going live on 5 July 2026 until 12 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for saved schedules. If you posted the exchange difference from one of these views at a second or later year end, compare it with the period movement shown now, and if you downloaded a schedule export with the FX Translation tab in the window above, generate it again. The currency panel now also asks for the rate at the prior year end so it can work out the movement for the year.

C-3 · 2026-07-11no engine change
Where: Disclosure note ledger boxes (short-term, low-value, variable payments, sublease income)

These boxes read European-style amounts with the separators swapped (5.000 was read as 5.00). Ledger amounts are typed fresh each time the note is built and are not stored, so no saved data was affected. The boxes now read amounts exactly like the calculator's own amount fields.

Affected input shape: Amounts typed with European separators (for example 5.000 meaning five thousand, or 1.234,56). Window: From the disclosure note going live on 5 July 2026 until 11 July 2026.

What to check: None. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook in the window above after typing a European-style ledger amount, generate it again.

C-2 · 2026-07-11no engine change
Where: Calculator CPI index input

A CPI index in the three-decimal shape was converted to a whole number before calculation (314.175 became 314175), overstating the index one thousand times. If a lease was calculated and saved with such an index, the saved schedule carries the converted number. The index is now passed to the engine exactly as typed, and an index containing a comma is stopped with a message asking for a dot decimal, because commas mean different things in different countries.

Affected input shape: A CPI index written with exactly three decimals (for example 314.175), or with a comma. Window: Until 11 July 2026.

What to check: Open any saved lease that has CPI events and check the index box shows the number you meant. If it shows something like 314175 where you meant 314.175, correct it, recalculate and save again.

C-1 · 2026-07-11no engine change
Where: Calculator currency panel (IAS 21 view); Disclosure note rate panel

An exchange rate in the affected shape was read as a thousands-grouped whole number (1.452 became 1452), so translated figures on these panels displayed up to one thousand times too large. Lease schedules in the lease's own currency were never affected. The rate boxes now read a separator as a decimal point on every rate field.

Affected input shape: An exchange rate written as a one-to-three digit whole number, a separator, then exactly three decimals (for example 1.452). Window: From the currency features going live on 5 July 2026 until 11 July 2026.

What to check: Nothing for saved schedules. These panels re-read the saved rate text, so affected displays corrected themselves the next time the lease was opened. If you downloaded a disclosure workbook with translated figures in the window above, generate it again.
